# EDGE GeoIntelligence Automation Agent

You are the **EDGE Weekly Critical Minerals Intel Agent** — an autonomous AI analyst and reporter running inside a Docker container on thepopebot. You approach tasks methodically, favor simplicity, and prioritize quality over speed.

Your purpose: Every Monday at 08:00 Ireland time, you autonomously execute the full EDGE Weekly Critical Minerals Intel pipeline — research → HTML report → Telegram delivery (as a file) → optional Google Drive upload → archival — without any human input.

## Identity & Persona

You are a senior strategic intelligence analyst for **EDGE**, an early-stage Irish deep-tech startup developing AI/ML geo-intelligence tools for Critical Minerals — specifically Rare Earth Elements (REE) and K–Th–U (potassium–thorium–uranium) prospecting. You write concise, actionable intelligence briefings for a very small startup team with limited time.

## Runtime Environment

Your workspace is `/home/coding-agent/workspace` — a live git repository.

### Temporary Files
Use `/tmp` for working files — downloads, screenshots, intermediate data, scripts, generated files. If a tool downloads a file, save it to `/tmp` and reference it directly.

Everything in the workspace `/home/coding-agent/workspace` is automatically committed and pushed when your job finishes. You do not control this. Be intentional about what you put here — **any file you create, move, or download into the workspace WILL be committed.**

### Directory Layout

- `agents/edge-critical-minerals/` — Your agent definition and job files.
- `agent-job/` — Runtime config, cron schedules (`CRONS.json`).
- `skills-library/` — Canonical skill source.
- `skills/` — Activation surface (symlinks to `skills-library/`).
- `data/`, `logs/` — Runtime data and job logs.

### Active Skills

{{skills}}

## Workflow on Trigger

When the cron job triggers you with the task described in `agents/edge-critical-minerals/jobs/weekly-report.md`, you must:

1. **Research** all 7 sections using your web search capabilities (WebSearch tool). Be thorough — verify dates, deadlines, amounts with live sources.
2. **Check git history** for any previous reports in this repo to understand what's been covered before, so you can prioritise new items and avoid repeating stale ones.
3. **Set fields** — compute report_date, week_number, filename.
4. **Build the styled HTML report** and save it to `/tmp/`.
5. **Send the HTML file to Telegram** using the Telegram Bot API (`sendDocument`). Include a summary caption.
6. **Try Google Drive upload** as a secondary/optional step (if credentials are available).
7. **Copy the HTML file** to `agents/edge-critical-minerals/reports/` for archival (auto-committed).

## Key Rules

- Never ask for input or clarification. Execute the full pipeline autonomously.
- If a step fails, retry once with a different approach, then fail with a clear error message.
- All web research must verify dates, deadlines, and amounts from live sources.
- Every item in the report must include a real, working URL.
- Write for a very small Irish deep-tech startup team with limited time.

1. Funding, Grants, and Investment Opportunities

Top Picks for EDGE

1. UK £50M Critical Minerals Investment Package — £25M Accelerator + £20M Magnet Hub (Announced 22 June 2026)
The UK government announced a major new critical minerals investment package today, including a £25M Critical Minerals Accelerator for collaborative projects across extraction, processing, and recycling, and a £20M Rare Earth Magnet Hub for developing, testing, and scaling rare earth magnet manufacturing. A demand aggregation platform (£5M) will help UK industry pool critical mineral purchasing power. Ireland-based EDGE should monitor cross-border consortium eligibility closely.

  • Funding Body: UK Government (Department for Business and Trade)
  • Stage: Accelerator (collaborative R&D) and Magnet Hub (infrastructure)
  • Ticket Size: £25M accelerator; £20M magnet hub; up to £5M demand platform
  • Why EDGE fits: Accelerator explicitly targets extraction and processing innovation; magnet hub addresses REE downstream value chain where EDGE's prospecting data has direct application
  • Eligibility: UK-based organisations; cross-border partnerships may apply
  • Deadline: Details to be announced via the Critical Minerals Delivery Team

The first cut-off for the RIS Innovation stream falls this Wednesday. Ireland qualifies for enhanced RIS terms with up to €1M per project (two-phase: €500K validation + €500K scale-up). Covers exploration, sustainable mining, and processing. The 16 October 2026 second cut-off remains available for consortia that cannot meet this week's deadline.

  • Funding Body: EIT RawMaterials
  • Stage: RIS Innovation (TRL 3→8)
  • Ticket Size: Up to €1M total per project
  • Why EDGE fits: Directly covers exploration innovation; Irish entities eligible for RIS-enhanced terms; AI/ML prospecting platform aligns with scope

The US Department of Energy's $69M accelerator program has Topic Area 2 closing this week: $6M for refining and alloying gallium, germanium, and silicon carbide for semiconductor applications. Topic Area 3 (Direct Lithium Extraction, $23M) closes 23 July 2026. While US-focused, the program signals the scale of US government commitment to critical minerals processing innovation.

  • Stage: Phase 1 prototype (TRL 3→6), Phase 2 pilot (TRL 6→7)
  • Ticket Size: Up to $2M Phase 1 (20% cost share); up to $8M Phase 2 (50% cost share)

Europe's leading battery raw materials gathering with 300+ senior leaders across the full battery supply chain: miners, processors, cathode/cell manufacturers, OEMs, recyclers, and policymakers. Focused on rare earth elements, lithium, cobalt, supply chain resilience, ESG, and geopolitics of critical materials. Senior leaders from mining, energy, defence, chemicals, and government sectors. A dedicated supply chain security focus distinguishes this from broader mining events.

Europe's premier critical minerals and mining investment event. Over 200 senior executives expected from 30+ countries. Covers rare earths, battery minerals, processing, exploration, financing, ESG, and clean energy technology. Co-located with LME Week and the MMTA Critical Materials Forum.

Opens 22 September 2026, deadline 2 February 2027. Focuses on novel processing technologies for critical raw materials extraction and beneficiation. Directly relevant to EDGE's AI/ML prospecting platform integration with downstream processing.

G7 Summit — Critical Minerals Alliance Launched (Évian, 17–19 June 2026)

G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance: At the 2026 G7 Summit in Évian-les-Bains, leaders announced a dedicated Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance to reduce dependence on any single supplier of rare earths and permanent magnets to below 60% by 2030 (with an ambition of 50%). The IEA will provide market monitoring and early warning of supply disruptions. Traceability and transparency pilot mechanisms will start with lithium and nickel, expanding to five new critical minerals each year. The G7 also agreed to explore joint procurement, price-gap subsidies, quotas, and price floors to support non-Chinese supply chains. 195 critical minerals projects have been announced since the start of 2026, representing €64 billion ($74 billion) in investment.

  • Jurisdiction: G7 (Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, UK, US, EU)
  • URL: US News — G7 Critical Minerals Alliance ↗

European Union — Three-Supplier Rule Drafted

EU Drafts "Three-Supplier Rule" for Critical Supply Chains (June 2026): The European Commission is drafting a mandatory "three-supplier rule" that would require companies in sensitive sectors to source critical components and raw materials from at least three different suppliers in different countries, with a single-supplier cap of ~30–40%. The rule covers critical raw materials, chemicals, EV batteries, rare earths, and pharmaceuticals. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič publicly announced the proposal on 5 June 2026. The rule would apply to large companies initially, with transition periods for SMEs. Discussions are expected at the EU leaders' summit. The rule faces WTO compatibility concerns from China and cost-burden criticism from industry.

  • Jurisdiction: European Union
  • URL: Reuters — EU Three-Supplier Rule ↗

EU CRMA Penalty Regimes Deadline — 24 November 2026: Member States must adopt penalty regimes for CRMA non-compliance by 24 November 2026, with administrative fines and potential withdrawal of strategic project status as enforcement mechanisms. The European Parliament's ITRE committee vote on CRMA amendments is scheduled for 24 June 2026.

UK Announces £50M Critical Minerals Package: The UK government announced a £50M ($66M) critical minerals investment package on 22 June 2026, including a £25M Critical Minerals Accelerator for collaborative extraction, processing, and recycling projects; a £20M Rare Earth Magnet Hub for manufacturing development and skills; and a £5M demand aggregation platform. This builds on £200M+ already committed and follows the opening of the UK's first commercial rare earth magnet plant in 25 years (HyProMag/Mkango in Birmingham). Industry Minister Chris McDonald announced the package during a visit to the Wilton Centre in Teesside.

  • Jurisdiction: United Kingdom

Yttrium Prices Remain at 100–150x Pre-Control Levels: China's April 2025 export controls on seven heavy rare earths (Sm, Gd, Tb, Dy, Lu, Sc, Y) continue to cause extraordinary price dislocation in ex-China markets. Rotterdam yttrium prices stand at ~$457.50/kg (vs ~$5.5K/tonne domestic Chinese price — a 100x+ spread). Dysprosium oxide trades at ~$1,450/kg externally (8x internal price); terbium at ~$4,500/kg (5x spread). Japan's Tosoh has suspended zirconia powder supply due to raw material shortages. Rare earth magnet exports from China fell 35% month-on-month in May 2026. Chinese brokerages (CITIC Securities, 22 June 2026) predict domestic supply tightness will persist with annual mining permit growth capped at 10%.

  • Jurisdiction: Global / China
  • URL: The Oregon Group — Rare Earth Price Surge ↗

China's New Mineral Resources Law Regulations (Effective 15 June 2026): China's revised Mineral Resources Law implementing regulations entered into force on 15 June 2026, designating 36 minerals (including REE, tungsten, lithium) as strategic resources. The regulations introduce national security reviews for foreign mining investments and fast-track strategic mineral reserve buildout, signalling even tighter state control over the critical minerals value chain.

  • Jurisdiction: China
  • URL: Canadian Mining Journal — China Mining Controls ↗

Scandinavia — European Rare Earth Development

Norway Fen Deposit — Government Takeover of Permitting (April 2026): The Norwegian government has taken over zoning and permitting responsibility for the Fen rare earth deposit in Telemark. The resource was upgraded by 81% to 15.9 million tonnes TREO, making it Europe's largest known deposit (~19% NdPr). First production targeted for late 2031. Thorium content in certain ore zones (rødberg carbonatite) remains a processing challenge; the preferred Fe-dolomite carbonatite ore type has lower thorium levels.

  • Jurisdiction: Norway
  • URL: NGU — Norway Rare Earth Minerals ↗

Sweden Norra Kärr — Government Decision Still Pending (June 2026): The Swedish Mining Inspectorate has recommended approval of the mining lease for Leading Edge Materials' Norra Kärr HREE project, with all government agencies recommending approval. However, the Swedish government has not yet issued its final decision. At Aktiedagarna 2026 (10 June), the company stated expectations for near-term resolution. The deposit is one of Europe's richest HREE sources (dysprosium, terbium, yttrium) with a 26-year mine life.

  • Jurisdiction: Sweden
  • URL: Globe and Mail — Norra Kärr Mining Lease ↗

Ireland — National Exploration Programme Update

Ireland's CRMA Exploration Programme Remains Behind Schedule: Geological Survey Ireland's CRMA-mandated national exploration programme continues to be delayed due to staffing shortages. Work is expected to begin in 2026 with the appointment of an entry-level geologist, with reporting during 2027. The Department may procure external services if needed. This persistent capacity gap strengthens the case for EDGE's AI/ML platform as a force multiplier for under-resourced geological surveys.

  • Jurisdiction: Ireland
  • URL: PA Media — Ireland Exploration Programme Delayed ↗

Strategic Context — EU Implementation Challenges

European Court of Auditors Warning on Diversification: The European Court of Auditors (February 2026) found that EU critical minerals diversification efforts have produced "no tangible results" so far, with domestic processing capacity declining. A joint policy brief from 11 Horizon Europe projects highlights that Europe's main risk is not resource scarcity but delayed implementation, with financing gaps for first-of-a-kind plants, fragmented regulatory practices, permitting complexity, and social acceptance challenges remaining key bottlenecks.

---

## 1. EIC Accelerator 2026 – "Boosting the European Critical Raw Materials Value Chain"

The **European Innovation Council (EIC) Accelerator** includes a dedicated Challenge for critical raw materials with a **€50 million budget** for 2026.

| Detail | Information |
|---|---|
| **Funding** | Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M equity per company |
| **TRL requirement** | From TRL 6 onwards |
| **Application process** | Step 1 (short proposal, 12-page form + pitch deck + 3-min video) → Step 2 (full proposal, max 20 pages) → Step 3 (jury interview in Brussels) |
| **2026 cut-off dates** | **7 Jan** | **4 Mar** | **6 May** | **8 Jul** | **2 Sep** | **4 Nov** 2026 |
| **Eligibility** | Single startups/SMEs/spin-outs established in EU or Horizon Europe Associated Countries. Small mid-caps (up to 499 employees) eligible for investment-only |
| **Key requirement** | For the Critical Raw Materials Challenge, grant-only beneficiaries must not be directly or indirectly controlled by a non-associated third country |

The evaluation now includes a **technical due diligence** step (online interview with an external technology expert) as part of the full proposal assessment, and interviews are limited to the top-ranked proposals (2–2.5× the available budget).

**Apply via**: `eic.ec.europa.eu` (Funding & Tenders Portal)

---

## 2. EIT Jumpstarter 2026 – Raw Materials Pre-Acceleration

A **7-month pre-acceleration programme** for early-stage innovators, powered by **EIT RawMaterials**. No equity required.

| Detail | Information |
|---|---|
| **Categories** | Mining & Exploration, Industrial Side Streams, Metals, Minerals, Sustainability |
| **Funding** | Up to **€10,000** for 1st place prizes (2nd: €5,000, 3rd: €3,000). Additional special prizes (€2,500) for Western Balkans, EU Outermost Regions, Rebuild Ukraine, New European Bauhaus |
| **Application deadline** | **17 May 2026** (23:59 CET) — some universities list **8 May 2026** as their internal deadline |
| **Applications open** | 13 March 2026 |
| **Eligibility** | Students, researchers, idea-holders from **EIT RIS-eligible countries**: Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Spain, plus EU Outermost Regions and several Associated Countries (Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Ukraine, Türkiye, etc.) |
| **Company status** | Teams with companies registered **before 1 Jan 2026** are not eligible. Startups registered in 2026 are eligible |

**Apply via**: `eitjumpstarter.eu`

---

For more established projects rather than early-stage startups, the **CRMA Strategic Projects** recognition is available. This is not an accelerator programme but a designation that can unlock permitting and funding advantages.

| Detail | Information |
|---|---|
| **Next cut-off** | **15 January 2026** (12:00 CET) |
| **Application** | Via EU Send WEB after requesting a communication channel via EU Survey |
| **Eligibility** | Any undertaking or consortium developing a raw material project (extraction, processing, recycling, or substitution) |

---

- **If you have an early-stage idea** (pre-revenue, pre-company): Apply to **EIT Jumpstarter** (deadline May 2026)
- **If you have a more mature startup/SME** (TRL 6+, some traction): Apply to the **EIC Accelerator Critical Raw Materials Challenge** (next cut-off 7 Jan, 4 Mar, or 6 May 2026)
- **If you have a larger extraction/processing project**: Consider **CRMA Strategic Projects** recognition

## June 2026 Rare Earth Prices — China Export Controls Impact

China's export controls on heavy rare earths, introduced in **April 2025** in response to US tariffs, continue to severely constrain global supply and drive prices sharply higher through **June 2026**. Here are the key data points across multiple sources:

### Ex-China Prices (Non-Chinese Market)

According to Argus data cited by Reuters, prices outside China have surged dramatically:

| Material | Pre-Control Price | May 2026 Price | Increase |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Yttrium oxide** | Single digits/kg | ~**US$1,100/kg** | **~140x** |
| **Dysprosium oxide** | ~US$300/kg | ~**US$1,450/kg** | **~4-5x** |
| **Terbium oxide** | ~US$1,000/kg | ~**US$4,500/kg** | **~350-450%** |

*(Source: The Oregon Group / Reuters)*

### Chinese Domestic Prices (June 2026)

China's Rare Earth Industry Association (CREIA) reported the **Rare Earth Price Index at 259.5–262.6** through late June 2026, roughly 2.6x the 2010 baseline. Domestic Chinese prices (converted to USD at ~¥7.15/US$1):

| Material | Chinese Domestic Price (June 22-26, 2026) |
|---|---|
| **Dysprosium oxide** | ~US$194–215/kg |
| **Dysprosium metal** | ~US$246–268/kg |
| **Terbium oxide** | ~US$896–973/kg |
| **Terbium metal** | ~US$1,107–1,213/kg |
| **Yttrium oxide** | ~US$7.70–8.25/kg *(but availability extremely constrained outside China)* |

*(Source: CREIA via Rare Earth Exchanges)*

### Supply Constraints

- **Exports of yttrium, dysprosium, and terbium** remain down ~50-60% compared to pre-April 2025 levels (Chinese customs data).
- **Near-zero Chinese exports of key heavy rare earths to Japan** in May 2026.
- Western buyers often face **prices several times higher** than Chinese domestic reference prices due to scarcity, delivery risk, and geopolitical premiums.

### Key Context

- China controls **~90% of global rare earth processing**.
- The seven restricted elements are: samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium, and yttrium.
- Chinese domestic prices reflect state-influenced market conditions (quotas, export licensing, strategic stockpiling), **not free-market equilibrium**.
- The ex-China market remains opaque, with most deals done via private bilateral contracts.

## EU Critical Raw Materials Act – 2026 Policy Update, Regulation & Ireland Strategic Projects

Here is a comprehensive summary of the latest developments based on the search results:

### 🔑 Key EU-Level Developments (2026)

1. **CRMA Entry into Force** – The Critical Raw Materials Act entered into force in **May 2024** and is directly applicable across all EU Member States. It identifies **34 critical raw materials (CRMs)** and **17 strategic raw materials (SRMs)**.

2. **2030 Benchmarks** – The Act sets binding targets for SRMs:
   - **10%** extraction within the EU
   - **40%** processing within the EU
   - **25%** recycling within the EU
   - No more than **65%** dependency on any single third country at any supply-chain stage

3. **60 Strategic Projects Selected** – The EU has approved 60 Strategic Projects focused on battery materials and EU processing capacity, benefiting from streamlined permitting and facilitated access to finance.

4. **RESourceEU Action Plan** – Adopted **December 2025**, this plan operationalises the CRMA through:
   - €3 billion in de-risked and blended finance
   - Coordinated raw material stockpiling
   - Joint purchasing mechanisms
   - Targeted export restrictions on waste and scrap streams
   - A proposed **European Critical Raw Materials Centre** (to be proposed by the European Commission in 2026)

5. **CRMA Amendments Proposed** – The European Commission tabled amendments in December 2025 to address geopolitical risks and implementation gaps. The **Council adopted its general approach in March 2026**, while the **European Parliament** is still preparing its position (likely advocating stronger circularity, binding recycled-content targets, and waste definitions). **Final agreement expected in 2027**.

6. **Member State Enforcement Deadline** – Member States must adopt **penalty regimes by 24 November 2026**.

---

### 🇮🇪 Ireland-Specific Measures & Strategic Projects

From the **Irish Government's Whole-of-Government Circular Economy Strategy 2026–2028** (public consultation document):

| Target | Requirement |
|--------|------------|
| **T26** | Ireland will adopt and implement national measures on circularity for CRMs in accordance with the EU CRMA, with a report to the European Commission **by 24 May 2026** and annually thereafter. |
| **T27** | Ireland will adopt measures to promote recovery of CRMs from extractive waste **by 24 November 2027**. |
| **T28** | Ireland will adopt measures to identify products containing permanent magnets within **two years** of implementing acts under the CRMA. |

**Mining & Exploration Projects in Ireland:**

- **Ballywire (PG West Project)** – Group Eleven Resources is exploring a **copper-silver-antimony system** in Ireland. Recent assay results from hole 26-3552-57 include high-grade intersections (e.g., 6.6m grading 83 g/t Ag, 1.60% Cu, 0.19% Sb), with antimony recognised as a critical/strategic mineral.

- **Ireland Strategic Investment Fund (ISIF)** – ISIF has committed **€30 million** to the Irish Minerals Fund, a vehicle dedicated to sustainable mining projects in Ireland, aligning with EU CRM objectives.

---

### ⚖️ Regulatory Compliance & Business Impact

- **"Large companies"** (500+ employees, >€150m turnover) using SRMs face additional obligations: risk assessments, supply chain diversification, and reporting.
- Export restrictions on **battery waste, black mass, magnet scrap, aluminium and copper scrap** are tightening.
- Penalties for non-compliance may include **turnover-based fines, market bans, and exclusion from strategic projects**.
- The CRMA operates alongside the **Net-Zero Industry Act** and a forthcoming **EU Circular Economy Act**.

### 📌 Outlook

The EU is moving from **policy signals to direct intervention** in critical raw material markets. CRMs are now treated as **economic security assets**, aligned with defence, trade, and industrial resilience strategies. For Ireland, the focus is on meeting circular economy obligations, developing extractive waste recovery, and leveraging strategic investment funds for mineral exploration.

| **T26** | Ireland will adopt and implement national measures on circularity for CRMs in accordance with the EU CRMA, with a report to the European Commission **by 24 May 2026** and annually thereafter. |
| **T27** | Ireland will adopt measures to promote recovery of CRMs from extractive waste **by 24 November 2027**. |
| **T28** | Ireland will adopt measures to identify products containing permanent magnets within **two years** of implementing acts under the CRMA. |

**Mining & Exploration Projects in Ireland:**

- **Ballywire (PG West Project)** – Group Eleven Resources is exploring a **copper-silver-antimony system** in Ireland. Recent assay results from hole 26-3552-57 include high-grade intersections (e.g., 6.6m grading 83 g/t Ag, 1.60% Cu, 0.19% Sb), with antimony recognised as a critical/strategic mineral.

- **Ireland Strategic Investment Fund (ISIF)** – ISIF has committed **€30 million** to the Irish Minerals Fund, a vehicle dedicated to sustainable mining projects in Ireland, aligning with EU CRM objectives.

---

### ⚖️ Regulatory Compliance & Business Impact

- **"Large companies"** (500+ employees, >€150m turnover) using SRMs face additional obligations: risk assessments, supply chain diversification, and reporting.
- Export restrictions on **battery waste, black mass, magnet scrap, aluminium and copper scrap** are tightening.
- Penalties for non-compliance may include **turnover-based fines, market bans, and exclusion from strategic projects**.
- The CRMA operates alongside the **Net-Zero Industry Act** and a forthcoming **EU Circular Economy Act**.

### 📌 Outlook

The EU is moving from **policy signals to direct intervention** in critical raw material markets. CRMs are now treated as **economic security assets**, aligned with defence, trade, and industrial resilience strategies. For Ireland, the focus is on meeting circular economy obligations, developing extractive waste recovery, and leveraging strategic investment funds for mineral exploration.

## UK Critical Minerals Policy: Latest Developments (June 2026)

Here's a summary of the key developments from June 2026:

### £50 Million Critical Minerals Programme Announced

On **22 June 2026**, Industry Minister **Chris McDonald** launched a new **£50 million ($66 million) Critical Minerals Programme** during a visit to the Wilton Centre in Teesside. This builds on over **£200 million** already committed to the sector. The programme is structured around three pillars:

| Pillar | Amount | Purpose |
|--------|--------|---------|
| **Magnet Hub** | Up to £20 million | National facility for rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing, skills, and training |
| **Critical Minerals Accelerator** | Up to £25 million | Support collaborative projects across extraction, processing, and recycling |
| **Demand Aggregation Platform** | Up to £5 million | Help industry consolidate demand, unlock investment, and secure supply through strategic partnerships |

### Key Context & Strategic Drivers

- **China dominance**: China accounts for ~70% of rare earth mining and ~90% of refining
- **National security framing**: The government explicitly ties critical minerals to economic and national security
- **Industrial Strategy alignment**: The programme sits within the broader "Vision 2035: Critical Minerals Strategy" published in November 2025

### Notable Milestones

- **First commercial rare earth magnet plant in 25 years** opened (HyProMag/Mkango Resources in Birmingham) — using recycled materials
- International partnerships being pursued with **the US and South Korea** on supply chains and processing capacity

### Industry Reactions

- **Critical Minerals Association**: Welcomed the shift from policy development to delivery
- **IOM3**: Highlighted the need for circularity, midstream capacity, and **skills development** (citing their report *The Talent Gap: Critical Skills for Critical Materials*)
- **ALFED** (Aluminium Federation): Welcomed aluminium's inclusion as both a Critical Mineral and Growth Mineral under Vision 2035, and advocated for greater emphasis on recycling and secondary materials

### What's Next

The Magnet Hub competition will launch first, followed by the Critical Minerals Accelerator, with market engagement on the Demand Aggregation Platform expected **later in summer 2026**. Programme details and guidance will be published on GOV.UK as each pillar opens.

# Norway Fen Rare Earth Deposit — June 2026 Update

Here is a summary of the key developments at the **Fen Carbonatite Complex** in Telemark, Norway, based on multiple reports from June 2026:

---

## 📈 Major Resource Expansion

The Fen deposit's total rare earth oxide (TREO) resource has **nearly doubled** from **8.8 million tonnes (2024) to 15.9 million tonnes (2026)** — an ~80–81% increase. This makes Fen the **largest known rare earth deposit in Europe**, surpassing Sweden's Per Geijer project.

- **Indicated resource:** 1.7 million tonnes (first indicated category established)
- **Inferred resource:** 14.2 million tonnes
- **Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr)** — critical for permanent magnets — makes up **~19%** of rare earth oxides in the indicated category
- Heavy rare earth elements (dysprosium, terbium) increased from ~0.1 Mt to **0.3 Mt**

## 🏛️ Norwegian Government Intervention

In **April 2026**, the Norwegian government **took over planning responsibility** for the Fen project from local authorities. Prime Minister **Jonas Gahr Støre** described the project as strategically important for Norway and European supply security.

The intervention came after **local land-use disputes** caused delays. Under national planning, zoning and development approvals are consolidated at the state level, reducing risks from objections and appeals.

## 🏭 Production Timeline

- **First production targeted:** Late **2031**
- **Annual NdPr output by 2032:** ~**800 tonnes per year**
- This would supply roughly **5% of projected EU demand** for NdPr
- The project remains pre-production; it still requires **full permitting, financing, and technical de-risking**

## 🌍 Strategic Context

- China controls ~75–85% of global rare earth mining and >90% of processing
- Europe currently has **no operating rare earth mines**
- Fen is positioned as a cornerstone of Europe's strategy under the **Critical Raw Materials Act**
- The REEsilience research project (2023–2026, NOK 16M) is developing sustainable processing technology, including thorium extraction for radiopharmaceuticals

## 🔑 Key Players

- **Operator:** Rare Earths Norway AS (CEO Alf Reistad)
- **Processing technology partner:** REEtec AS
- **Thorium/medical partner:** Thor Medical AS
- Norway is not an EU member but is part of the **European Economic Area (EEA)** and a close NATO ally

---

*Sources: EuroMining News, Mining South East Europe, Reuters, Norwegian Research Council, NGU (Geological Survey of Norway)*

## Sweden Norra Kärr Mining Lease Decision 2026 — Latest Update

The **Swedish Government has granted a 25-year mining lease (Exploitation Concession) for the Norra Kärr heavy rare earth elements project**, as announced on **June 28, 2026**.

### Key Timeline in 2026

| Date | Milestone |
|------|-----------|
| **March 10, 2026** | Swedish Mining Inspectorate (Bergsstaten) **recommended approval** and submitted the application to the Swedish Government for a final decision |
| **April 19, 2026** | Government **still holding the decision**; company directors exercised options injecting CAD $788,000 |
| **June 10, 2026** | Leading Edge Materials presented at Aktiedagarna 2026, expecting a near-term resolution |
| **June 28, 2026** | ✅ **Government granted the 25-year Exploitation Concession** |

### What Was Approved

- **Company:** Leading Edge Materials Corp. (via its wholly-owned Swedish subsidiary GREENNA Mineral AB)
- **Lease type:** 25-year Exploitation Concession (Sw. *bearbetningskoncession*) for Norra Kärr K Nr. 2
- **Deposit significance:** One of Europe's richest rare earth element deposits, with a particularly high proportion of **dysprosium, terbium, and yttrium** — heavy rare earth elements (HREEs) critical for permanent magnets in EVs, wind turbines, and defense applications

### Government's Rationale

The Swedish Government concluded that **supplying Sweden and Europe with these critical raw materials clearly outweighs competing land-use interests**, citing:

- No REE production currently exists anywhere in the EU
- The deposit's strategic importance for the green energy transition
- European supply chain resilience and reduced dependence on China

### Next Steps for the Project

1. **Environmental permitting** under the Environmental Code
2. **Updated Pre-Feasibility Study (PFS)** expected in H2 2026
3. **Offtake agreements and financing** discussions
4. Potential reapplication for **Strategic Project designation** under the EU Critical Raw Materials Act

### Local Context

The project has faced **local opposition** over concerns about potential impacts on Lake Vättern (a major drinking water source) and local environmental values. The company has committed to developing the mine to the highest environmental standards and maintaining dialogue with the community. The project design was revised to remove chemical processing from the mine site, reducing its environmental footprint.

**Energy and Industry Minister Ebba Busch (KD)** stated that the deposit could satisfy a large portion of Sweden's and the EU's supply needs for these strategically important materials.

## Search Results: Canada-Australia Critical Minerals Strategy & Policy Announcements (2026)

Here is a summary of the key findings from the web search:

### Major Bilateral Announcement — March 5, 2026

Canadian Prime Minister **Mark Carney** traveled to Sydney and Canberra, Australia — the **first bilateral visit by a Canadian PM to Australia in nearly two decades**. He met with Australian PM **Anthony Albanese** and addressed the Australian Parliament.

### Key Agreements on Critical Minerals

1. **Australia joins the G7 Critical Minerals Production Alliance** — a Canada-led initiative launched under Canada's 2025 G7 Presidency to expand critical minerals production, processing capacity, and diversify supply chains from mine to market.

2. **Alignment of strategic stockpiles** — Australia's A$1.2 billion **Critical Minerals Strategic Reserve** will be more closely aligned with **Canada's Defence Stockpiling Regime**.

3. **Combined production power** — Canada and Australia together produce:
   - ~1/3 of global **lithium** and **uranium**
   - >40% of global **iron ore**

4. **New Clean Energy Partnership** — to catalyze trade and investment, scale up clean energy technologies, and modernize electricity grids.

### Other Cooperation Areas Announced

- **Investment mobilization** — Australian institutional investor IFM announced intention to invest up to **$10 billion** in Canada; Canadian and Australian pension/superannuation funds deepening collaboration
- **Defence & security** — new biannual Defence Ministers Meetings; collaboration on Arctic Over-the-Horizon radar system (Australia's largest defence export)
- **AI** — cooperation between Australian and Canadian AI Safety Institutes
- **Mining Skills Exchange Pilot** — addressing labour shortages in critical minerals extraction and digital mining technologies
- **Tax treaty modernization** — negotiations to lower barriers for two-way investment

### G7 Critical Minerals Declaration — June 17, 2026

The G7 (with Australia as a partner country) issued a leaders' declaration on securing critical minerals supply chains, including:

- Setting a target to reduce dependency on a single supplier for **rare earths and permanent magnets to under 60% by 2030**, with ambition to reach 50%
- Announcing **195 projects** since early 2026 reaching **€64 billion in investment**
- Establishing a new **G7 Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance** (building on the Canada-launched Production Alliance)
- Commitment to traceability pilots for **lithium and nickel**, expanding to five new minerals per year
- Advancing **recycling targets** and **circular economy** approaches

### Strategic Context

Both nations are positioning as **"middle powers"** seeking to diversify supply chains away from China's dominant control over critical mineral production and processing. As Carney stated: *"In a world of great power rivalry, middle powers have a choice: compete for favour or combine for strength."*

For further details, the primary official source is the **[Joint Press Conference Transcript](https://www.pm.gov.au/media/press-conference-parliament-house-canberra-45)** from the Australian PM's office, and the **[G7 Leaders' Declaration](https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/statements/2026/06/17/g7-leaders-declaration-securing-supply-chains-critical-minerals)** on the Canadian PM's site.

Here is a summary of key news on Ireland's critical minerals exploration and mining from June 2026:

## Major Drilling Results at Ballywire (Group Eleven Resources) — 11 June 2026

**Group Eleven Resources Corp.** reported exceptional new assay results from its **Ballywire discovery** at the 100%-owned PG West Project in Ireland. These are some of the highest copper grades seen in Ireland in 60 years.

- **Drill hole 26-3552-57** intersected nine zones of copper-silver mineralization, including:
  - **0.6m at 23.60% Cu, 506 g/t Ag, 2.04% Sb** (antimony)
  - 2.8m at 5.09% Cu, 110 g/t Ag, 0.44% Sb
  - 6.6m at 1.60% Cu, 83 g/t Ag, 0.19% Sb
  - Previously announced: **62.5m at 5.6% Zn+Pb** and 25 g/t Ag from the upper zone

- CEO Bart Jaworski said the 23.60% copper result "represents some of the highest copper grades attained by any operator over the last 60 years of modern mineral exploration history in Ireland."
- The deeper Cu-Ag mineralization has now been intersected across **430m of strike length** across four drill fences.
- Four rigs are active at Ballywire, with the drilling program expanded from 20,000m to **67,000–75,000m** following a C$12M financing in March 2026.
- The overall discovery spans approximately **3.2 km** along a 6 km prospective trend.

## Unicorn Mineral Resources — Kilmallock Gravity Survey

**Unicorn Mineral Resources** reported results from 3D gravity modelling at its **Kilmallock project** (Limerick Basin), identifying five fault-controlled density anomalies along the Rathdowney Trend, near Group Eleven's Ballywire deposit. The company is launching an expanded 340-station gravity survey to refine drill targets.

## Boliden Tara Deep — Exploration Tunnel Approved

**Boliden Tara Mines** received planning permission from Meath County Council to extend an underground exploration tunnel by **3 km at ~1 km depth** to assess the viability of the **Tara Deep ore body** (current inferred resource: 27 million tonnes). If commercial, this could extend the mine's life for decades, though a new tailings pond would be needed. The mine's licences were recently extended to **2045**.

## PERC/IGI Training Event on Critical Raw Materials — 4 June 2026

The **Institute of Geologists of Ireland (IGI)** and **PERC** co-organised a training event in Dublin on resource classification and reporting using **UNFC and CRIRSCO**, including sessions on the **EU Critical Raw Materials Act** and its implications for Irish and European mineral projects.

## Research Publication — Lithium Pegmatites in SE Ireland

A June 2026 paper in *Mineralium Deposita* by Kaeter and Menuge examined the use of **columbite-tantalite and cassiterite** as indicator minerals for lithium pegmatites in **southeast Ireland**, with implications for lithium exploration in the Leinster pegmatite belt.

## Regulatory Context (EU Level)

A June 2026 article noted that the **EU Critical Raw Materials Act** sets 2030 targets of at least **10% domestic extraction**, **40% EU processing**, and **25% recycling** of strategic raw materials. Irish exploration activity is increasingly evaluated on whether commodities (e.g., copper, antimony, zinc) align with these strategic priorities.

## G7 Critical Minerals Alliance — June 2026 Implementation Update

### Summit Overview
At the **G7 Leaders' Summit in Évian-les-Bains, France** (June 15–18, 2026), G7 leaders announced a major expansion of their **Critical Minerals Resilience and Production Alliance**, originally launched under Canada's G7 Presidency in 2025. The summit produced a joint statement on critical minerals supply chain security, with Australia also joining the alliance.

### Key Targets
- **Reduce reliance** on any single non-G7 supplier of rare earths and permanent magnets to **under 60% by 2030**, with an ambition to reach **50% as soon as possible**
- Focus on diversifying supply chains from **mine to market**

### New Institutional Mechanisms
1. **IEA-led monitoring platform** — A new coordination platform backed by the International Energy Agency to:
   - Monitor critical mineral markets
   - Issue early warnings of supply disruptions
   - Track supply chain vulnerabilities

2. **Harmonized stockpiling mechanisms** — Starting with **lithium and nickel** as pilot minerals, expanding to five new minerals per year (with emphasis on rare earths)

3. **G7-wide traceability framework** — For tracking minerals throughout supply chains

### Financial Commitments
- **$5 billion+** unlocked through 13 new partnerships and initiatives announced at the summit (across 8+ countries)
- The alliance is now catalyzing **$19.2 billion** in critical minerals projects through **69 partnerships**
- Since the start of 2026, G7 countries have announced **195 projects** totaling **€64 billion ($74 billion)**

### Notable Deals Announced
| Partner Countries | Projects |
|---|---|
| **Canada–Germany** | Sio Silica & RCT Solutions — high-purity silica project in Manitoba |
| **Canada–Japan** | KAP Minerals & Hanwa Co. — critical minerals processing in Ontario |
| **Canada–Italy** | Eni investing $95M in Nouveau Monde Graphite's Matawinie Mine (Québec) |
| **Canada–France** | Torngat Metals & Schneider Electric — Strange Lake rare earth project (Nunavik) |
| **Canada–Japan** | Ucore Rare Metals & Sumitomo Corp. — rare earth separation facility (Kingston, Ontario) |
| **Canada–Denmark** | Danish Export Credit Agency $275M guarantee for First Phosphate mine (Québec) |

### Policy Tools Being Explored
- **Price-gap subsidies**
- **Joint procurement instruments**
- **Quotas and price floors** (via plurilateral trade agreements)
- **Price support mechanisms** (e.g., potential reference pricing via DARPA's OPEN system)
- U.S. expected to propose legally binding deals with Japan and the EU

### Context & Motivation
The initiatives are a direct response to **China's dominance** — Beijing controls ~90% of global rare earth processing and ~70% of production. Export controls imposed by China in 2025 on rare earth permanent magnets disrupted Western supply chains, prompting accelerated action.

*Sources: Reuters, Government of Canada, EE News, Mining Digital, Anadolu Agency, U.S. News & World Report*

- **Rare Earths Norway** reported an **~81% increase** in resource estimate — now **15.9M tonnes TREO** (JORC-compliant), nearly doubling from 8.8M tonnes in 2024.

- **LKAB** advancing a **critical minerals industrial park in Luleå** (environmental permit received), processing rare earths & phosphorus from iron ore residual streams.

## Major Developments (June 2026 & Recent)

### 1. 🇮🇹 RarEarth (Italy) – €2.5M Grant + up to €6M Equity (June 2026)
- **Milano/Ancona-based startup** selected by the European Innovation Council (EIC) in **June 2026** as the only Italian startup among 38 European companies to receive funding
- **Grant of €2.5M** plus opportunity for up to **€6M equity investment**
- Will use funds to build its **first production plant** for recovering rare earths from end-of-life motors and e-waste
- Awarded the **"STEP Seal"** for strategic technologies

### 2. 🇮🇹 Italy – EU's First Industrial-Scale Rare Earth Recycling Plant (Ceccano)
- **LIFE 22ENV-IT-INSPIREE project** – construction of EU's first industrial-scale plant in **Ceccano, Frosinone province**
- Processes rare earth elements from **electrical/electronic waste (WEEE)**
- Initial capacity: **20 tonnes/year of permanent magnets** → fully operational: **up to 2,000 tonnes/year** (producing 500-700 tonnes of high-purity rare earth compounds)
- Uses advanced **hydrometallurgical processes** developed by University of L'Aquila
- EU co-funding of **€3.2M** via LIFE Programme (42-month implementation)

### 3. 🇳🇱 Paladin Envirotech – Netherlands Expansion (Helmond) – June 2026
- **June 18, 2026**: Announced expansion into **Helmond, Netherlands** via acquisition of R&L Recycling
- Strategic hub for recovering/processing critical materials within EU
- Total global investment to date: **$85M**
- Deploying **RECapture** and **Critical Minerals Recycling (CMR)** technology across allied markets
- EU Critical Raw Materials Act targets: limit reliance on single third country to **65% of supply by 2030**

### 4. 🇩🇪 Mkango/HyProMag – Pforzheim, Germany (April 2026)
- **April 28, 2026**: Official opening of rare earth magnet recycling & manufacturing plant in **Pforzheim, Germany**
- Fully permitted for **up to 750 tonnes/year** of NdFeB magnets and alloys
- First commissioning runs of HPMS (Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap) reactor completed
- Initial capacity: **~100 tonnes/year**, scaling to **~350 tonnes/year**, targeting **750 tonnes/year** within 3 years
- Supported by **European Regional Development Fund** and **Baden-Württemberg Ministry**

### 5. 🇩🇪 Mkango/Remloy – Bitterfeld, Germany (May 2026)
- **May 20, 2026**: Mkango agreed acquisition of **Remloy** (Heraeus Amloy Technologies) for **€8M**
- Plant in **Bitterfeld, Germany** recycles magnets via melting process (produces NdFeB alloy powders for bonded/hot-deformed magnets)
- Fully commissioned with **500 tonnes/year** production capacity
- Stockpile of **>300 tonnes** of rare earth magnets and alloys
- First commercial sales targeted by **end of 2026**

### 6. 🇬🇧 Mkango/HyProMag – Birmingham, UK (April 2026)
- Advancing commercial-scale recycling at **Tyseley Energy Park, Birmingham**
- Supplied recycled NdFeB magnets to **Siemens** for SIMOTICS servomotor rotor (presented at Hannover Messe, April 2026)
- **9.2 tonnes** of recycled NdFeB alloy powder produced since commissioning; **7.4 tonnes shipped** to customers
- Evaluating phased expansion: from **100–350 tonnes/year** up to **1,000 tonnes/year**

---

**Summary:** June 2026 is proving to be a pivotal month for European rare earth magnet recycling, with **RarEarth's EIC grant** and **Paladin's Netherlands expansion** leading new investment announcements, alongside the operational ramp-up of Mkango's multiple German and UK facilities. The EU's **Critical Raw Materials Act** is the primary policy driver behind these investments.

1. Funding, Grants, and Investment Opportunities

Top Picks for EDGE

1. EIC Accelerator — Critical Raw Materials Challenge (€50M) — Step 2 Cut-off 8 July 2026 (9 days away)
The EIC Accelerator's dedicated "Boosting the European Critical Raw Materials Value Chain" Challenge has a Step 2 full proposal cut-off in 9 days on 8 July 2026. With €50M available and grants up to €2.5M (plus up to €10M equity), this is the most directly accessible single-SME funding pathway for EDGE's AI/ML prospecting platform. Italian startup RarEarth was selected in the June 2026 cohort with €2.5M grant for rare earth recycling — confirming CRM challenge payouts are active. September and November cut-offs provide fallback opportunities.

  • Funding Body: European Innovation Council (EIC)
  • Stage: TRL 6→8/9 (Step 1 short proposal, Step 2 full proposal, Step 3 jury interview)
  • Ticket Size: Up to €2.5M grant + up to €10M equity investment
  • Why EDGE fits: Direct single-SME pathway with dedicated CRM thematic panel; Irish SME eligibility; Step 1 can be submitted continuously
  • Eligibility: Single SME established in EU or Horizon Europe Associated Country
  • Deadline: Step 2 cut-offs: 8 July, 2 September, 4 November 2026
  • URL: Segler Consulting — EIC Accelerator 2026 Deadlines

This Innovation Action opens on 22 September 2026 with a deadline of 2 February 2027. With a €49M total budget, it covers the full CRM value chain from exploration through processing and recycling. At TRL 5–7 with ~€6–8M per project, this is a strong consortium-based opportunity for EDGE's AI/ML platform integrated with EU downstream partners.

  • Funding Body: European Commission — Horizon Europe Cluster 4

  • Deadline: 2 February 2027 (opens 22 September 2026)
  • URL: Euramaterials — CL4-2027-01 MAT-PROD Overview

3. EIT RawMaterials KAVA Call 14 — RIS Innovation (Final Cut-off 16 October 2026)
Following the 24 June first cut-off, the final cut-off for the RIS Innovation stream is 16 October 2026. Ireland remains eligible for enhanced RIS terms with up to €1M per project (two-phase: €500K validation + €500K scale-up). Covers exploration, sustainable mining, and processing with TRL 3→8 range. The 16 October deadline provides ample time for consortium building.

  • Stage: RIS Innovation (TRL 3→8)
  • Ticket Size: Up to €1M total per project
  • Why EDGE fits: Directly covers exploration innovation; Irish entities eligible for RIS-enhanced terms; AI/ML prospecting platform aligns with scope
  • Eligibility: Min 2 organisations from different RIS countries; knowledge triangle representation
  • Deadline: 16 October 2026 (final cut-off)
  • URL: Innovation Place — KAVA 14 RIS Innovation

Additional Opportunities

  • EIC Pathfinder Challenges 2026 (€96M, deadline 28 October 2026): Grants up to €4M at 100% funding rate. The Advanced Materials for Miniaturised Energy Harvesting challenge targets reduced CRM dependency. Open to consortia (min 3 partners). URL: Innovate UK — EIC 2026 Overview
  • EIC Transition Open 2026 (€100M, deadline 16 September 2026): Single cut-off for maturing research results toward market readiness. Up to €2.5M per project. Open to single SMEs and consortia. Suitable for taking TRL 3–4 geoscience AI research toward commercial application. URL: Luxinnovation — EIC Transition 2026

Energy and Industry Minister Ebba Busch stated the deposit could satisfy a large portion of Sweden's and the EU's supply needs. All government agencies and the Mining Inspectorate had recommended approval. The company now proceeds to environmental permitting, updated pre-feasibility study, and offtake/financing discussions. Targets reducing reliance on any single supplier of rare earths and permanent magnets to below 60% by 2030 (ambition: 50%). The IEA will provide market monitoring and early warning. Traceability pilots start with lithium and nickel, expanding to five new minerals annually. Since early 2026, 195 critical minerals projects have been announced totalling €64 billion ($74 billion) in investment. A new European Critical Raw Materials Centre is to be proposed in 2026. CRMA amendments are being negotiated, with the Council adopting its general approach in March 2026 and Parliament preparing its position. Final agreement expected in 2027.
